mainTopic: Collecting from and appraising a pregnant cow's calf, and the משנה on items brought into another's courtyard
overview: This amud finishes רבא's explanation of a cow that gored and gave birth. If the cow is gone, only a quarter of the damage is collected from the calf, because we are not sure the calf was inside her when she gored. The גמרא shows this fits רבא's view that a fetus counts as part of the mother's body, while a hen's egg does not. רבא then teaches that damage to a pregnant cow and her unborn calf is appraised as one unit, so the damager is not overcharged. The same method is used for a slave's cut hand and a damaged field. רב אשי explains that the damager can say, "I harmed a pregnant cow, so value a pregnant cow." When the cow and calf have different owners, the fat goes to the cow's owner, and the הלכה is that they split the pregnancy bulk. A new משנה then rules that permission decides who pays when pots or produce are brought into another person's courtyard. The משנה's third case, about an ox, begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the cow is gone, a quarter is paid from the calf
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רבא's explanation: when the goring cow is not available, the injured party collects only רביע נזק from the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the cow is not here, a quarter of the damage is paid from the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's explanation of the משנה. If the cow that gored cannot be found, the injured party may collect only a quarter of the damage from her calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full damage owed for a first-time goring is חצי נזק. Since we are not sure the calf was part of the cow when she gored, the calf can only be held for half of that half, which is a quarter. This is how רבא reads the משנה's 'quarter' payment.

phrases.english: If the cow is not here,
phrases.notes: This finishes a statement of רבא that started just before: if the cow is here, the payment comes from her.

phrases.english: a quarter of the damage is paid from the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation of the משנה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the cow is unavailable and it is unclear whether the calf was in her at the time of goring, only רביע נזק is collected from the calf.

steps.title: Inference: if the calf was surely inside her, the full half is paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבא's words that the quarter payment comes only from doubt. If we know the calf was a fetus at the goring, the whole חצי נזק can be collected from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that we do not know whether the calf was with her when she gored or not. But if it is clear to us that the calf was with her when she gored, the full half damage is paid from the calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבא's ruling. The 'quarter' only happens because of doubt, so if we knew the calf was inside the cow, the full חצי נזק would come from the calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quarter payment is a compromise for a ספק (doubt). Take away the doubt, and it becomes clear that רבא treats the calf just like the cow itself, so the full amount can be collected from it. This sets up the next step, which shows רבא holds this elsewhere too.

keyTerms.meaning: With her (here: inside her as a fetus)

steps.confusionAlert: 'With her' does not mean the calf was standing next to her. It means the calf was still inside her as a fetus when she gored.

phrases.english: The reason is that we do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוָה וָלָד בַּהֲדַהּ כִּי נְגַחָה,
phrases.english: whether the offspring was with her when she gored
or whether it was not;
but if it is obvious to us
that the offspring was with her when she gored,
the entire half damage is paid from the offspring;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the reason behind רבא's quarter payment in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבא, the calf is fully liable like its mother. The quarter payment comes only from doubt about whether it was a fetus at the time of goring.

steps.title: This fits רבא's ruling about calves versus eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the inference matches another statement of רבא: you can collect from a damaging cow's calf because it is her body, but not from a damaging hen's egg because it is just a secretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: a cow that caused damage, the injured party collects from her calf. Why? It is her body. A hen that caused damage, he does not collect from her egg. Why? It is just a secretion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא is consistent. Elsewhere he rules that a calf that was inside a cow when she did damage can be used for payment, because it counts as part of her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus grows as part of the mother's body, so it is included in the 'body of the damager' that payment comes from. An egg is something the hen gives off, like a discharge, not part of her body, so it cannot be taken for her damages. This backs up the inference in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his other view)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, a fetus is part of the mother, so damages can be collected from it. An egg is only a secretion, so they cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: Payment for an ox's first-time damage comes only from the body of the damaging animal. So the question of what counts as 'her body' decides what the injured party can take.

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
A cow that caused damage, he collects from her offspring.
phrases.notes: He means a calf that was still inside the cow when she did the damage.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is her body.
A hen that caused damage, he does not collect from her egg.
What is the reason? It is merely a secretion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the inference of step 2 by showing רבא holds the same principle elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: The inference that, for רבא, the full חצי נזק can be collected from a calf known to have been a fetus at the goring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own ruling that one collects from a damaging cow's calf (גופה היא) but not from a hen's egg (פירשא בעלמא).

steps.title: Appraise the calf together with the cow
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching of רבא: when damage is done to a pregnant cow and her calf, בית דין appraises them as one unit and does not value each separately, so the damager is not overcharged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: we do not appraise the cow by herself and the calf by itself. Rather, we appraise the calf together with the cow. Because if you don't say this, you end up hurting the one who caused the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבא about how to measure damage. When an ox hurts a pregnant cow and her unborn calf dies, the loss is measured as the drop in value of a pregnant cow, not as two separate items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live calf on its own is worth more than the extra a cow is worth just for being pregnant. Charging for the cow and calf separately would make the damager pay more than the real loss to the owner. So we measure the whole pregnant cow as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who caused the damage

steps.whatToRemember: Damage to a pregnant cow and her fetus is measured as one unit, the loss in value of a pregnant cow, so the damager is not overcharged.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Weakening the damager' does not mean hurting his animal. It means making him pay more money than he really owes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general rule of appraisal: we measure the real loss to the owner's property as a whole, not the sum of its parts.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
We do not appraise the cow by herself
and the offspring by itself;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁמִין לַוָּלָד עַל גַּב פָּרָה.
phrases.english: rather, we appraise the offspring together with the cow.
For if you do not say so,
you will end up weakening the damager.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related teaching of רבא about damages involving a pregnant cow, this time about how to measure the damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage to a pregnant cow and her fetus is appraised as one unit (the calf together with the cow), not separately, so the damager does not pay more than the true loss.

steps.title: The same one-unit appraisal applies to a slave's hand and a damaged field
steps.stepSummary: רבא's principle of appraising the damage as part of the whole is applied to cutting off a slave's hand and to damaging part of someone's field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you find the same rule when someone cuts off the hand of another person's slave. And you find the same rule when someone damages another person's field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's rule of appraising the damaged item as part of the whole is not new. The same method is used in two other damage cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slave's hand, we do not ask how much the owner would charge to let the hand be cut off. We measure how much less the whole slave is now worth. With a field, we do not value the eaten patch alone. We measure how much the whole field lost, which usually comes out to a smaller payment.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who caused the damage
And similarly you find (the same rule in another case)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that appraising damage as part of the whole is a general method in נזיקין, not a special rule for pregnant cows.

phrases.english: And similarly you find this
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבא's rule from the last step: value the damage as part of the whole.

phrases.english: with one who cuts off the hand of another person's slave.
And similarly you find this
with one who damages another person's field.
phrases.notes: He damaged only part of the field, so the loss is measured against the whole field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's one-unit appraisal rule from Step 4 to parallel cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a slave's cut hand and in a damaged field, the loss is measured by the drop in value of the whole, not by valuing the damaged part alone.

steps.title: Why protect the damager if separate valuation is the real law?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: if valuing cow and calf separately is the true law, then the damager should simply pay the higher amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: If that is the law, then let the damager lose out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the reason given for רבא's rule. That reason was that we should not overcharge the damager.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given was that valuing each part separately would hurt the damager. רב אחא asks why that matters. If separate valuation is really the correct law, the damager should pay the higher amount and accept the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: And if that is the law
Let him become weakened (let him lose money)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי:
But if that is the law,
phrases.notes: He means: if the correct law is to value the cow and the calf separately.

phrases.english: let the damager be weakened!
phrases.notes: Literally 'let him grow thin'. He means: let him pay more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְאִי דִּינָא הוּא, לִיכְחוֹשׁ מַזִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רבא's rule in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that separate valuation would unfairly 'weaken' the damager.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fairness to the damager is not a reason to change the law. If separate valuation is correct, the damager should simply pay it.

steps.title: The damager says: I harmed a pregnant cow, so value a pregnant cow
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that separate valuation is not actually the law. What was damaged is one thing, a pregnant cow, so it is valued as one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the damager can say to him: I damaged a pregnant cow for you, so I will value a pregnant cow for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the cow and calf are valued together. The damager has a fair claim that what he harmed was a single item: a pregnant cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not just about being kind to the damager. Separate valuation is simply the wrong measurement. A pregnant cow is one item for sale, so the loss is the drop in the value of 'a pregnant cow'.
steps.whatToRemember: A pregnant cow is appraised as one unit because that is what was damaged. It is not valued as a cow plus a separate calf.

phrases.english: Because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The damager is speaking to the owner of the cow.

phrases.english: I damaged a pregnant cow of yours,
so I will value a pregnant cow for you.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the reason: valuing as one unit is the correct law, not a favor to the damager.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate valuation is the true law, and the one-unit method only protects the damager.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thing damaged was a pregnant cow, so it is appraised as one unit.

steps.title: Cow and calf with different owners: who gets the pregnancy bulk?
steps.stepSummary: The cow's extra fat obviously belongs to the cow's owner. The גמרא asks who gets the extra value from the pregnancy 'bulk'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if the cow belongs to one person and the calf to another, the value of the fat goes to the cow's owner. What about the bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about splitting the payment between two owners. It states the obvious part first and then asks about the unclear part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Extra fat on the cow's body is clearly the cow's, so it goes to her owner. The 'bulk', the fuller look of a pregnant cow that raises her price, comes from carrying the calf. So it is unclear whose it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Fatness (extra fat on the cow from the pregnancy)
Bulk / swelling (the fuller look of a pregnant cow)

steps.confusionAlert: פיטמא and נפחא are two different kinds of extra value. The fat is clearly the cow's. Only the bulk is in question.

phrases.english: It is obvious: if the cow belongs to one person and the calf to another,
the fat goes to the owner of the cow.
What about the bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, פָּרָה דְּחַד וּוָלָד דְּחַד – פִּיטְמָא לְבַעַל פָּרָה. נִפְחָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the one-unit appraisal and asks how to divide it between two owners.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who gets the payment for the pregnancy bulk when the cow and calf have different owners?

steps.title: רב פפא and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא disagree about the bulk
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the bulk goes to the cow's owner. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the two owners split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it goes to the owner of the cow. רב אחא, the son of רב איקא, said: they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question about the bulk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא treats the bulk as part of the cow's body, like the fat. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא sees it as coming from both the cow and the calf it carries, so the owners share it.

phrases.english: רב פפא said: it goes to the owner of the cow,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר: חוֹלְקִין.
phrases.english: רב אחא, the son of רב איקא, said: they divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְבַעַל פָּרָה, רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר: חוֹלְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא: all to the cow's owner. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא: the two owners split it.

steps.title: The הלכה: the owners split the bulk
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב אחא בריה דרב איקא: the payment for the bulk is divided between the cow's owner and the calf's owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on the dispute and follows the view that the owners split the bulk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat goes fully to the cow's owner. The bulk, which comes from both the cow and the calf she carries, is shared by the two owners.
steps.whatToRemember: When the cow and calf have different owners, the fat goes to the cow's owner, and the bulk is split between both owners.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: they divide it.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The payment for the pregnancy bulk is split between the cow's owner and the calf's owner.

steps.title: The potter who brings his pots into someone's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on pots brought into a בעל הבית's courtyard. Without permission, the בעל הבית is פטור if his animal breaks them, and the potter is חייב if the pots hurt the animal. With permission, the courtyard owner is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A potter brought his pots into a homeowner's courtyard without permission, and the homeowner's animal broke them. The homeowner is exempt. If the animal was hurt by the pots, the owner of the pots must pay. But if the potter brought them in with permission, the owner of the courtyard must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It gives its first case: pots brought into another person's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on whether the potter had רשות to be there. Without permission, the pots don't belong in the courtyard, so the בעל הבית owes nothing for breaking them, and the potter pays if they injure the animal. With permission, the בעל הבית has agreed to have them there, so he is חייב if his animal damages them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
The homeowner, the owner of the courtyard
Exempt from paying / liable to pay

steps.confusionAlert: In the first line, the one who is פטור is the בעל הבית whose animal broke the pots, not the potter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole משנה: permission to bring items in decides who carries the risk of damage.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A potter who brought his pots
into a homeowner's courtyard without permission,

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁבְּרָתַן בְּהֶמְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and the homeowner's animal broke them: he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הוּזְּקָה בָּהֶן – בַּעַל הַקְּדֵרוֹת חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: And if it was injured by them, the owner of the pots is liable.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הִכְנִיס בִּרְשׁוּת – בַּעַל הֶחָצֵר חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: But if he brought them in with permission, the owner of the courtyard is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקַּדָּר שֶׁהִכְנִיס קְדֵרוֹתָיו לַחֲצַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The cow-and-calf discussion ended at step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רשות, the בעל הבית is פטור for his animal breaking the pots, and the potter is חייב for injuries the pots cause the animal. With רשות, the courtyard owner is חייב.

steps.title: The same rule for produce brought into the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same rule to produce. Without permission, the בעל הבית is פטור if his animal eats it, and the produce owner is חייב if the animal is hurt by it. With permission, the courtyard owner is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone brought his produce into a homeowner's courtyard without permission, and the homeowner's animal ate it. The homeowner is exempt. If the animal was hurt by the produce, the owner of the produce must pay. But if he brought it in with permission, the owner of the courtyard must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case with the same rule. This time the items are produce instead of pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only new detail is the kind of damage. The animal eats the produce instead of breaking it. The permission rule stays exactly the same, which shows it works for any kind of item and any kind of damage.

phrases.english: If one brought his produce
into a homeowner's courtyard without permission,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲכָלָתַן בְּהֶמְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and the homeowner's animal ate them: he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הוּזְּקָה בָּהֶן – בַּעַל הַפֵּירוֹת חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: And if it was injured by them, the owner of the produce is liable.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הִכְנִיס בִּרְשׁוּת – בַּעַל הֶחָצֵר חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: But if he brought them in with permission, the owner of the courtyard is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִכְנִיס פֵּירוֹתָיו לַחֲצַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rule of step 11 with produce instead of pots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רשות, the בעל הבית is פטור if his animal eats the produce, and the produce owner is חייב if it injures the animal. With רשות, the courtyard owner is חייב.

steps.title: Opening of the third case: an ox brought into the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a third case, an ox brought into a בעל הבית's courtyard without permission. The case is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone brought his ox into a homeowner's courtyard without...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is starting its third case, about an ox, and stops mid-sentence. It is setting up a ruling that comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pots and produce are lifeless objects, but an ox is a living animal that can cause damage by itself. The opening matches the earlier cases, so expect the same permission-based framework to be applied to it.

phrases.english: If one brought his ox
into a homeowner's courtyard without
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here. It continues on the next amud with "permission" and the ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the third parallel case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet given. The case is set up here and its ruling comes on the next amud.
